description:
## Supplement counter-research to bd JMAP-zx3s.6: workspace canonical pattern for creation-id keys is String, not Id.

The main review filed bd JMAP-zx3s.6 (\"MdnSendRequest.send keyed by String, not Id — type discipline divergence from on_success_update_email\"), arguing that \`MdnSendRequest.send: HashMap<String, Mdn>\` should be \`HashMap<Id, Mdn>\` for consistency with the diff's new \`on_success_update_email: HashMap<Id, PatchObject>\`. The reviewer's own calibration explicitly flagged this finding as \"least confident\" pending verification of the prevailing pattern across the workspace.

This supplement resolves the uncertainty. The workspace canonical pattern is established in \`crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:282-286\` (SetResponse):

\`\`\`rust
/// Failed creates, keyed by caller-supplied creation id.
pub not_created: Option<HashMap<String, SetError>>,   // String for creation-ids
/// Failed updates, keyed by record id.
pub not_updated: Option<HashMap<Id, SetError>>,       // Id for real ids
/// Failed destroys, keyed by record id.
pub not_destroyed: Option<HashMap<Id, SetError>>,     // Id for real ids
\`\`\`

The pattern is unambiguous: creation-id-keyed maps use \`String\`; real-id-keyed maps use \`Id\`. The justification is that \`Id\` (per \`crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:20-29\`) carries the contract \"URL-safe base64 alphabet, max 255 octets\" — creation-id reference syntax (\`#k1\`) does not conform and would lie about the type's contract if used as the key.

\`MdnSendRequest.send\` keys are creation IDs (clients assign them; the server matches them in the response's \`sent\` / \`notSent\` maps). They are not real Email IDs. So \`HashMap<String, Mdn>\` is correct per workspace canonical pattern, and the .6 recommendation reverses.

### What this means for the wider .6 finding

1. \`MdnSendRequest.send\`: \`HashMap<String, Mdn>\` is CORRECT — no change needed. Close .6 as wontfix.
2. \`MdnSendResponse.sent\`: \`HashMap<String, Mdn>\` is CORRECT (same creation-id key).
3. \`MdnSendResponse.not_sent\`: \`HashMap<String, Value>\` is CORRECTLY keyed but INCORRECTLY typed in its value — see bd JMAP-zx3s.10 for the SetError typing fix.
4. \`MdnSendRequest.on_success_update_email\`: the diff's choice of \`HashMap<Id, PatchObject>\` is the actual divergence — see bd JMAP-zx3s.11 for the underspecification issue (Id contract vs \`#creationId\` references).

### Why I'm filing this as a separate finding rather than commenting on .6

Per the \`/review-library-supplement\` template, every finding is filed as a \`bd create\` issue under the epic. The counter-research changes the maintainer's correct path forward on .6 (close as wontfix rather than \"convert HashMap<String, Mdn> to HashMap<Id, Mdn>\"), so it is worth a separate, searchable bead rather than buried inline in .6's comment thread.

### Cross-references

- bd JMAP-zx3s.6 — original finding this counter-research contradicts.
- bd JMAP-zx3s.10 — typed-value fix for not_sent (SetError vs Value).
- bd JMAP-zx3s.11 — underspecification of on_success_update_email's Id keys.
- \`crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:282-286\` — workspace canonical SetResponse pattern.
- \`crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:20-29\` — Id contract definition.
title: Counter-finding to JMAP-zx3s.6: SetResponse canonical pattern uses HashMap<String, T> for creation-id keys — recommendation reverses
